rationale: A 24-year-old Indian male presenting with fever was diagnosed with P. vivax malaria. During post-treatment follow-up, thick blood film revealed microfilariae identified morphologically as Wuchereria bancrofti, and molecular PCR targeting the cox1 gene with BLAST sequence analysis confirmed W. bancrofti. The patient was successfully treated with albendazole and ivermectin. E1 confirmatory evidence satisfies VPD criteria.

evidence_items.source_quote: The parasites illustrated in Figures 1(a)-1(k) were identified as MF of Wuchereria bancrofti based on their morphological characteristics such as presence of sheath unstained or lightly stained with Giemsa stain (Figures 1(a), 1(c), and 1(j)), cephalic space proportions (Figures 1(a)-1(c), 1(e), and 1(f)), and tail that tapers to delicate point without nucleus at the tip
Comparison of the sequences using Basic Local Alignment Tool (BLAST) confirmed the identity of the MF as W. bancrofti.

rationale: A 45-year-old female presented with an adnexal mass. Surgical excision and intraoperative cytological examination of the ovarian cyst fluid revealed microfilariae in a hemorrhagic background alongside malignant epithelial cells, establishing a final diagnosis of mucinous cystadenocarcinoma of the ovary with coexistent microfilaria. Direct microscopic detection of microfilariae provides E1 confirmatory evidence.

evidence_items.source_quote: Cyst fluid was haemorrhagic on gross examination and on microscopy three dimensional clusters of cells with smooth outline were visualized. These cells had large hyperchromatic nucleus with scant cytoplasm. An occasional microfilaria was identified in the haemorrhagic background
On the basis of fluid cytology, gross, histopathological and immunohistochemical findings a final diagnosis of "Mucinous cystadenocarcinoma of ovary with microfilaria in ovarian cyst fluid" was made.

rationale: A 17-year-old female presented with a painful subcutaneous swelling in the left arm. Fine needle aspiration cytology yielded purulent material containing numerous microfilariae displaying characteristic hyaline sheath, cephalic space, and tail devoid of nuclei diagnostic of Wuchereria bancrofti. The patient responded promptly to diethylcarbamazine (DEC). Direct cytological demonstration of W. bancrofti provides E1 confirmatory evidence satisfying VPD.

evidence_items.source_quote: Cytological examination of Giemsa-stained smear showed a large number of microfilaria in the background of degenerated inflammatory cells that comprised of neutrophils, eosinophils, histiocytes, and lymphocytes. The microfilaria had typical features of the presence of hyaline sheath, cephalic space, and tail end devoid of nuclei. Thus, these Wuchereria belonged to the species bancrofti [Figure 1].
The patient was treated with diethylcarbamazine [100 mg ter die sumendum (TDS)] for 21 days and kept on follow-up. The swelling subsided by the end of the 3rd week.

rationale: An 18-year-old female from Uttar Pradesh presented with vulval elephantiasis. Although buffy coat microscopy was negative for microfilariae, filarial antigen serology was positive, and the patient responded favorably to ivermectin. E2 strong evidence (circulating filarial antigen positivity) in an endemic setting with typical chronic genital lymphedema satisfies the diagnostic criteria for lymphatic filariasis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Subsequent to histopathologic report, filarial antigen serology was done, which was positive. The patient was put on ivermectin, and she responded well.

rationale: A 30-year-old renal allograft recipient had an enlarged iliac lymph node excised during transplantation. Histopathology demonstrated coiled adult worms of Wuchereria bancrofti within necrotic lymphatics, and DEC challenge subsequently provoked microfilariae in peripheral blood. E1 confirmatory histopathological and parasitological evidence satisfies VPD criteria.

evidence_items.source_quote: Histopathology of the lymph node revealed necrotic lymphatic filled with coiled adult worms of Wuchereria bancrofti (microfilaria) (Fig 1) with double uteri in female worms. Subsequently after diethylcarbamazine citrate (DEC) challenge test, his peripheral blood also showed microfilarial worms (Fig 1)
evidence_items.test_name: Lymph node histopathology and DEC challenge test
evidence_items.target_concept: Wuchereria bancrofti adult worms and microfilariae
evidence_items.specimen: iliac lymph node and peripheral blood

rationale: A 35-year-old male presented with a massive retroperitoneal cyst. Cytological examination of centrifuged cyst fluid revealed numerous microfilariae morphologically consistent with Wuchereria bancrofti, histopathology showed dead and calcified parasites in the cyst wall, and DEC provocation demonstrated microfilariae in peripheral blood. Direct demonstration provides E1 confirmatory evidence.

evidence_items.source_quote: Giemsa-stained smears of the cyst fluid revealed many microfilariae morphologically consistent with Wuchereria bancrofti [Figure 2]. The cyst wall on histopathological examination revealed multiple dilated lymphatic spaces. Dead and calcified forms of the parasite surrounded by inflammation and foreign body reaction could be seen in the wall [Figure 3]. The patient was administered diethylcarbamazine as a provocative maneuver and subsequent examination of the peripheral blood smear also revealed microfilariae.
evidence_items.test_name: Cyst fluid cytology, histopathology, and DEC blood smear
evidence_items.specimen: retroperitoneal cyst fluid, cyst wall, and peripheral blood

rationale: A 55-year-old female presenting with breast cancer and axillary lymphadenopathy was found to have sheathed microfilariae of Wuchereria bancrofti on fine needle aspiration of the lymph node, coexisting with metastatic adenocarcinoma deposits. Demonstration of diagnostic morphology (hyaline sheath, tail tip free of nuclei) provides E1 confirmatory evidence of filariasis.

evidence_items.source_quote: However, the lymph node aspirate showed sheathed microfilariae along with tumor cells [Figure 1a and b]. Wuchereria bancrofti was identified by the presence of hyaline sheath, multiple coarse, discrete nuclei extending from the head to tail and the tail tip free of nuclei [Figure 1b].
evidence_items.test_name: Fine needle aspiration cytology of lymph node

rationale: A 38-year-old female presented with an isolated left axillary swelling. Fine-needle aspiration cytology revealed multiple sheathed, coiled microfilariae of Wuchereria bancrofti in a background of lymphocytes and eosinophils, and the swelling responded to diethylcarbamazine. Direct microscopic cytodiagnosis provides E1 confirmatory evidence.

evidence_items.source_quote: The smears revealed multiple sheathed, coiled, slightly curved mf of bancrofti with the prominence of lymphocytes along with the presence of few eosinophils in a proteinaceous background [Figures 2a and b]. On FNAC, a diagnosis of filarial parasitic infestation was made.

rationale: A 55-year-old male with leprosy presented with peripheral neurological weakness. Incidental microfilariae seen on slit-skin smear were definitively confirmed by nocturnal (10 pm) thick and thin blood smears demonstrating multiple sheathed microfilariae of Wuchereria bancrofti with absence of nuclei at the tail tip. Treated with DEC. Confirmatory nocturnal smear provides E1 evidence.

evidence_items.source_quote: After the patient was admitted, both thick and thin blood smears were made from blood samples collected at 10 pm. Microscopic examination of Giemsa-stained smears showed multiple sheathed Mf with an absence of nuclei at the tail tip (Fig. 3). A diagnosis of asymptomatic filariasis caused by W. bancrofti was made and the patient was initiated on diethylcarbamazine (DEC) at a dose of 6 mg/kg/day in divided doses.
evidence_items.test_name: Nocturnal thick and thin blood smear microscopy

rationale: A 42-year-old male with an intra-abdominal retroperitoneal cyst and scrotal hydrocele underwent FNAC, which aspirated fluid revealing live microfilariae of Wuchereria bancrofti, followed by positive DEC provocation on blood smear and histological confirmation in the excised cyst. Direct visualization of live parasites provides E1 confirmatory evidence.

evidence_items.source_quote: A fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) was obtained. Chocolate-colored fluid was aspirated, which revealed live microfilariae of Wuchereria bancrofti on microscopic examination [Figure 5]. The patient was administered diethylcarbamazine as a provocative maneuver. Subsequent peripheral blood smear demonstrated motile microfilariae, confirming our diagnosis.
evidence_items.test_name: FNAC and DEC provocation peripheral blood smear
evidence_items.specimen: retroperitoneal cyst aspirate and peripheral blood

rationale: A 46-year-old male presented with a giant retroperitoneal cystic mass. Histopathology of the excised cyst wall revealed microfilaria fragments with lymphatic dilation, and the filariasis immunochromatographic test (ICT, Alere BinaxNOW) for Wuchereria bancrofti was positive. The patient was treated with DEC. Histological demonstration (E1) and specific antigen detection (E2) confirm the diagnosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Histopathology of the cyst revealed a unilocular cyst with walls composed of fibro-collagenous tissue lined by flattened epithelium and focal areas of calcification along with a few fragments of microfilaria (Fig. 4). The features were suggestive of a lymphatic cyst of filarial origin. The postoperative recovery of the patient was uneventful and was given diethylcarbamazine therapy (100 mg t.i.d. for 3 weeks). Further, filariasis immunochromatographic test (ICT) by Alere  BinaxNOW  Filariasis kit for Wucheria bancrofti was positive.
evidence_items.test_name: Cyst histopathology and Alere BinaxNOW ICT antigen test
evidence_items.target_concept: Wuchereria bancrofti microfilariae and filarial antigen

rationale: A 30-year-old female with ureteric calculus had incidental live sheathed microfilariae identified in centrifuged urine sediment, confirmed as Wuchereria bancrofti on Giemsa staining and DEC provocation testing. The patient was cured following DEC therapy. Microscopic demonstration of live microfilariae provides E1 confirmatory evidence.

evidence_items.source_quote: Microscopic examination of centrifuged sediment of the urine showed 15-20 pus cells/high power field (hpf), 2-3 epithelial cells/hpf, and 300-400 RBCs/hpf, which were normal in morphology. A single live intact-sheathed microfilaria was seen wriggling under the coverslip [Video 1]. Giemsa-stained smears of the urine revealed microfilariae with intact sheath and absence of nuclei in the cephalic space and pointed tail section which led to a diagnosis of W. bancrofti
evidence_items.test_name: Urine sediment microscopy and Giemsa staining

rationale: A 65-year-old male presented with gross painless hematuria. Urine cytology revealed sheathed microfilariae of Wuchereria bancrofti characterized by absence of nuclei at the tip of the tail, and the patient became completely asymptomatic following a 21-day course of diethylcarbamazine. Direct cytological demonstration of microfilariae provides E1 confirmatory evidence.

evidence_items.source_quote: Smears of the first patient revealed predominantly RBCs with occasional benign urothelial cells and polymorphs. Occasional sheathed microfilaria (Mf) larvae with the absence of nuclei at tip of the tail (W. bancrofti) were also noted. The smear was negative for malignant cells. The patient was prescribed diethylcarbamazine (DEC) course for 21 days following which he became asymptomatic.

rationale: A 36-year-old male from eastern India presented with paroxysmal nocturnal dry cough, marked peripheral eosinophilia (37,510/microL), strikingly elevated total serum IgE (9915 U/L), bilateral pulmonary reticulonodular opacities, and a positive anti-filarial antibody by immunochromatography. He achieved complete clinical cure after 3 weeks of diethylcarbamazine therapy. The patient satisfies all diagnostic criteria for tropical pulmonary eosinophilia (occult lymphatic filariasis), providing E2 strong evidence.

evidence_items.source_quote: Serum immunoglobulin (Ig) E level was 9915 U/L (reference range: less than 150 U/L).
evidence_items.target_concept: Elevated IgE in tropical pulmonary eosinophilia

evidence_items.source_quote: Anti-filarial antibody was positive by the immunochromatographic method.
The patient was started on DEC therapy at a dose of 100 mg thrice daily. Cough improved within three days of treatment initiation and the fever subsided after five days.
evidence_items.target_concept: Favorable response to DEC in TPE

rationale: A 73-year-old male with a remote history of travel to Barbados (endemic for Wuchereria bancrofti in the 1970s) and chronic hydrocele presented with progressive scrotal and suprapubic lymphedema. Two filariasis serologies were positive, leading to a definitive diagnosis of chronic lymphatic filariasis. In non-endemic travelers presenting with chronic genital lymphedema, positive filarial serology (E2) establishes the diagnosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Finally, two filariasis serologies returned positive. The diagnosis of lymphatic filariasis (LF) was made in 2020 (Figure 2).

rationale: A 48-year-old male presented with cervical lymphadenopathy. Fine-needle aspiration cytology revealed metastatic squamous cell carcinoma coexisting with microfilariae of Wuchereria bancrofti, displaying characteristic hyaline sheath and pointed tail devoid of terminal nuclei. Direct cytological demonstration of W. bancrofti provides E1 confirmatory evidence.

evidence_items.source_quote: The filarial worm is smoothly curved, covered with a hyaline sheath and a pointed tail. The body has multiple discrete evenly spaced nuclei with no terminal nuclei in the tail. The microfilaria is identified as Wuchereria bancrofti owing to characteristic smoothly curved worm with pointed tail, devoid of nuclei (Figure 1)

rationale: A 43-year-old male from Sudan presented with severe milky urine (chyluria) for one year. Examination of a peripheral blood smear confirmed the presence of filarial parasites, and retrograde pyelogram identified a left pyelo-lymphatic fistula, successfully treated with povidone-iodine sclerotherapy and ivermectin. Direct blood smear demonstration provides E1 confirmatory evidence.

evidence_items.source_quote: Ether was added to a test tube filled with the cloudy urine rendering the mixture clear suggesting chyluria, A peripheral blood smear confirmed the presence of filarial parasites (Fig. 1).
